Archival Dispatch: 12 Master Broadcasts Dated Across Glenn Miller, Henry Morgan, Adele Clark, Eddy Arnold, and Abroad with the Lockharts

Batch 83 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 83 recovers and dates 12 historical broadcasts spanning big band swing interviews, biting radio satire, jazz torch vocals, country music government transcriptions, historical frontier drama, and early international travelogues: an intimate February 1940 interview where Paul Douglas questions swing king Glenn Miller regarding his Chesterfield Moonlight Serenade signature arrangements on The Glenn Miller Orchestra, 2 classic satirical broadcasts from dry-witted comedian Henry Morgan on The Henry Morgan Show (1947, dissecting the origins of money and dog horoscopes), 3 warm vocal performances by Adele Clark on Adele Clark Sings (ABC, 1945), 3 musical public service transcriptions by country music superstar Eddy Arnold backed by the Charles Ryan Quartet on Eddy Arnold Time (1952), frontier development in the American southwest on The American Trail (1953), and 2 chapters of European tourism comedy starring Gene and Glenn Lockhart in Abroad with the Lockharts (1934).

1. Glenn Miller & The Henry Morgan Show (1940–1947)

Swing orchestra milestones and postwar razor-sharp comedy satire:
